# Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4

{
  "abstract_verbatim": "For every fixed $`1\\le q\\lt 4`$, critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge as ordered curves to chordal $`\\mathop{\\mathrm{SLE}}\\nolimits _{\\kappa(q)}`$, where $`\\kappa(q)=4\\pi/\\arccos(-\\sqrt q/2)`$, confirming the Rohde–Schramm prediction in this parameter range. This holds in every bounded Jordan domain under uniform marked boundary approximation. The complete nested plane loop collections converge to whole-plane $`\\mathop{\\mathrm{CLE}}\\nolimits _{\\kappa(q)}`$ in a spherical matching topology retaining multiplicities and traversals. At <i>q</i> = 1 we obtain Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> For every fixed $`1\le q\lt 4`$, critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge as ordered curves to chordal $`\mathop{\mathrm{SLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$, where $`\kappa(q)=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)`$, confirming the Rohde–Schramm prediction in this parameter range. This holds in every bounded Jordan domain under uniform marked boundary approximation. The complete nested plane loop collections converge to whole-plane $`\mathop{\mathrm{CLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$ in a spherical matching topology retaining multiplicities and traversals. At <i>q</i> = 1 we obtain Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.

- **claim-main-interfaces-loops** (theorem, [source](#stmt-intro-main)): For every fixed real $1\le q<4$, the following assertions hold.* 1. *For every bounded Jordan domain $D$ with distinct boundary marks $a,b$, and every approximation satisfying <a href="#intro:marked-jordan" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:marked-jordan">[intro:marked-jordan]</a>, the Dobrushin strand $\eta_n$ converges in law, in <a href="#intro:curve-metric" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:curve-metric">[intro:curve-metric]</a>, to chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ from $a$ to $b$ in $D$.* 2. *Under the specified free infinite-volume law, $\Gamma_\delta$ converges in law as $\delta\downarrow0$ to the nested whole-plane $\operatorname{CLE}_{\kappa(q)}$, in the spherical collection topology just defined. The limit is Möbius invariant.* *Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence. No uniformity in $q$ is asserted.
  - Explanation: For each fixed cluster weight in the stated range, the Dobrushin interface converges to chordal SLE and the full free-plane loop collection converges to nested whole-plane CLE.
- **claim-cardy-bond** (theorem, [source](#stmt-intro-cardy)): Let $\psi:D\to\mathbb H$ send $a,c,d$ to $0,1,\infty$, and put $x=\psi(b)\in(0,1)$. Under the boundary and approximation conventions above, $$\label{intro:cardy-formula} \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P(C_n) =\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^x[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\mathrm dt} {\displaystyle\int_0^1[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\mathrm dt}.$$
  - Explanation: Square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges has crossing probability converging to Cardy's integral formula.
- **claim-bond-exponents** (theorem, [source](#stmt-intro-bond-exponents)): For every fixed $k\ge1$ and every sufficiently large fixed $r$, $$\label{intro:bond-arm-exponents} \pi_1(R)=R^{-5/48+o(1)},\qquad \pi_{2k}(r,R)=R^{-(4k^2-1)/12+o(1)} \qquad(R\to\infty).$$ Moreover, $$\label{intro:bond-thermodynamic-exponents} \begin{aligned} \theta(p)&=(p-\tfrac12)^{5/36+o(1)} &&(p\downarrow\tfrac12),\\ \chi(p)&=\|p-\tfrac12\|^{-43/18+o(1)} &&(p\to\tfrac12,\ p\ne\tfrac12),\\ \xi(p)&=\|p-\tfrac12\|^{-4/3+o(1)} &&(p\to\tfrac12,\ p\ne\tfrac12). \end{aligned}$$
  - Explanation: Arm exponents and thermodynamic exponents of square-bond percolation follow from the loop limit.
- **claim-loop-law** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-loop-law)): On a genus-zero tile surface with positive cap completions, the switch weight $d^\ell$, where $\ell$ counts completed medial loops, is proportional to the critical FK weight with the corresponding boundary partition. Conditional laws on common subdomains are therefore FK laws with induced partitions. The same assertion holds after interchanging the colors. On a torus without caps the two weights differ by a factor bounded in terms of $q$ alone.
  - Explanation: Capped tile switch weight is proportional to the critical FK weight with the induced boundary partition.
- **claim-finite-loops** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-finite-loops)): For every fixed $1\le q<4$, all medial strands of the specified free infinite-volume square FK law are almost surely finite loops. Finite deterministic surgeries admit positive normalized loop laws with the FK conditional laws of Lemma <a href="#prelim:loop-law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:loop-law">4</a>.
  - Explanation: All medial strands of the free infinite-volume law are almost surely finite loops.
- **claim-collar-density** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-collar)): Suppose two positive laws have the same graph in a collar between radii $r$ and $16r$. In this collar the graph is a full annulus, or a bounded number of sectors separated by straight coordinate walls; coincident slit banks are allowed. Their deterministic wire portions agree there. Only boundedly many wire blocks traverse the collar, and no other identifications jump it. One radial side faces an arbitrary unknown partition, whereas the graph and deterministic wires toward the other side are fixed. The marginal densities on edges beyond that other side are mutually bounded by a constant independent of scale and of the far graph. Equivalently, their expectations of every nonnegative remote function are comparable with this same constant.* *The conclusion also holds for a fixed-shape rectangular bulk collar shielding a long box, with a constant depending on its shape.
  - Explanation: Across a collar, remote marginal densities under different unknown-side partitions are comparable by a scale-independent constant.
- **claim-relative-collar** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-relative-collar)): Under the hypotheses of Lemma <a href="#prelim:collar" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prelim:collar">6</a>, suppose successive collars have one of the following geometries:* 1. *a full annulus, or one sector whose through wires are precisely continuous primal wire portions along its side rays;* 2. *two sectors, with primal wires along both side rays of one sector and no through wires in the other, and no further fixed contacts between the sectors.* *After $m$ further collars of a sufficiently large fixed radius ratio, the remote expectations of every fixed nonnegative function under two possible unknown-side laws have ratio $1+O((1-c)^m)$, or both expectations vanish. The conclusion holds in either radial direction, also after positive modifications or tilts supported on the unknown side.
  - Explanation: Repeating collars makes remote expectations under two unknown-side laws agree up to a geometrically small relative error.
- **claim-passage-moments** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-passages)): In any fixed buffered annulus or sector of the preceding types, a raw passage count $X$ satisfies $$\label{prelim:passage-moment} \mathbb E[\exp(BX)\mid\text{exterior}]\le C_B \qquad(0\le B<\infty),$$ uniformly in scale and in exterior states inducing the specified graph and arbitrary boundary partition. The same holds for a fixed finite family of macroscopic passage counts in a fixed geometry.
  - Explanation: Raw passage counts have uniformly bounded exponential moments of every order.
- **claim-local-tilts** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-tilts)): For fixed $b>0$, put $$F_j=\mathbb E b^{N_j},\qquad d\nu_j=F_j^{-1}b^{N_j}\,d\mathbb P.$$ The ratios $F_j/F_{j-1}$ are bounded above and below uniformly. Under $\nu_j$, the shell counts $X_i$ at and beyond the outer tilt level, $i\ge j$, have all fixed exponential moments uniformly bounded. The assertions remain conditional on exterior data of the specified geometry and allow adjoining a fixed family of passage counts with buffers at or beyond that level.
  - Explanation: Local nest tilts have bounded normalizing ratios and keep shell passage counts exponentially integrable.
- **claim-absorb-errors** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-absorb)): Suppose $Y_n\ge0$, $\mathbb E Y_n\ge n^{-A}/C$, and $\mathbb E Y_n^2\le Cn^A$, whereas $X_n\ge0$ has uniformly bounded exponential moments at every fixed rate. For fixed $C_0\ge1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, $$C_\varepsilon^{-1}n^{-\varepsilon} \le \frac{\mathbb E[Y_n C_0^{\pm X_n}]}{\mathbb E Y_n} \le C_\varepsilon n^{\varepsilon}.$$
  - Explanation: Multiplying by exponentials of a lightly-tailed count changes expectations by at most an arbitrarily small power of n.
- **claim-surface-factorization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prelim-surface)): Let finitely many straight finite wall segments have fixed macroscopic shapes and positive mutual separation. Complete each as a positive isolated boundary slit. Let $Z_s$ be its partition function relative to the unmodified plane law, and $Z_{\rm all}$ the corresponding partition function with all slits. Uniformly in the mesh, $$\label{prelim:surface-factorization} Z_{\rm all}\asymp\prod_s Z_s.$$ Reversing every cap-wire polarity on both banks of a straight isolated segment with boundedly many changes alters $Z_s$ by a bounded factor. The same comparison holds for a segment and its image, with transported cap data, under a symmetry of the homogeneous tile lattice, with the two color names exchanged when the symmetry exchanges the color lattices.
  - Explanation: Partition functions of separated slits factorize up to constants.
- **claim-local-costs** (theorem, [source](#stmt-exp-local-costs)): Changing a cutoff radius by a fixed factor, changing the fixed compatible exterior completion, applying a tile-lattice symmetry to the experiment, or interchanging both color names and wire designations changes each of these logarithms by $O(1)$. The expectations of the local weights, their fixed powers, and the same arm indicator have logarithms of size $O(\log n)$. For some $c>0$, $$\label{exp:strict-arm} P(n)\le-c\log n+O(1).$$
  - Explanation: Local logarithmic costs are stable under convention changes and the arm cost decays strictly.
- **claim-three-log-comparisons** (theorem, [source](#stmt-exp-comparisons)): With the definitions above, $$\begin{aligned} 2P+2D_*+4(C_0+C_1)&\le o(\log n),\label{exp:rectangle-budget}\\ C_0+C_1+L_0+L_1&\le o(\log n),\label{exp:corner-budget}\\ P+\sum_j\log\frac{F_-(a_j)}{F_+(a_j)} &\le o(\log n),\label{exp:charge-budget} \end{aligned}$$ where the finite list of fixed charges in the last inequality satisfies <a href="#exp:charge-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="exp:charge-range">[exp:charge-range]</a> and $\sum_j a_j=1$.
  - Explanation: Three logarithmic budget inequalities hold for rectangle, corner and charged geometries.
- **claim-cap-elimination** (theorem, [source](#stmt-exp-cap-elimination)): For disk arcs whose boundary intervals contain at most one wire flip, their positive cap-loop factors are $d$ for a zero-flip high starting port and $1$ for a zero-flip low starting port or a one-flip arc, up to a bounded overall loop-count error and an error $d^{O(X)}$ for remaining macroscopic arcs. A nest of $N$ straddling arcs at a corner of turn $g\pi$ without a wire flip has negative-expansion weight relative to its caps comparable to $f(g)^{N/2}$.
  - Explanation: Disk arcs with at most one flip eliminate against caps with explicit loop factors.
- **claim-polygon-budget** (theorem, [source](#stmt-exp-polygon-budget)): Let a fixed simple rectilinear polygon have $m$ concave and $m+4$ convex true corners, with wire changes in side interiors. It has tile approximants differing by $O(1)$ mesh units such that at least $\lfloor m/2\rfloor$ corners of each relative wire type occur in each of the convex and concave sets, also after global wire reversal. For these approximants, $$\label{exp:polygon-saving} 3P+D_*+\sum_{v\,\mathrm{convex}}C_{i(v)} +\sum_{v\,\mathrm{concave}}L_{i(v)} \le\frac12P-\frac32D_*+o(\log n).$$ Each fixed family of negative endpoint charges with magnitudes summing to one has total wrong-to-correct local logarithmic cost at most $-P+o(\log n)$.
  - Explanation: Balanced corner parities give a strictly saving logarithmic budget for rectilinear polygons.
- **claim-angular-estimate** (theorem, [source](#stmt-bulk-angular-estimate)): Fix a compact interval $I\subset(-v,v)$. Let $B_{\rm in}$ be a product of $P_\zeta$ rows and $B_{\rm out}$ a product of $P_\xi$ rows, at real angles in $[-v,v]$. Suppose each product contains at least $n\ge1$ angles in $I$. Uniformly for $x,y\in[-v,v]$, $$\begin{aligned} \\|B_{\rm out}N(x)B_{\rm in}\\|&\le Cn^{-1+\rho}, \label{bulk:low-estimate}\\ \\|B_{\rm out}\{N(x)-e^{i\tau(x-y)}N(y)\}B_{\rm in}\\| &\le Cn^{-1-\rho}.\label{bulk:high-estimate} \end{aligned}$$ The constant depends on $q$ and $I$. Boundedly many additional pairs of before-twist rows may be inserted immediately to the right of $N$, and additional pairs of after-twist rows immediately to its left. The two terms in <a href="#bulk:high-estimate" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="bulk:high-estimate">[bulk:high-estimate]</a> may use different such insertions; on each side their counts must be even. The constant may depend on a bound for these counts. Multiplication of $D$ by a common scalar multiplies the bounds by its absolute value.* *The same estimates hold in the physical square array sliced in a diagonal time direction: its time angles are $\pm\gamma_0$, where $\gamma_0=\pi/4$, and its space angles alternate between $\pi-\gamma_0$ and $\gamma_0$. The exterior states may contain any finite number of physical row and spin insertions outside the sandwich. A scalar contraction is bounded by the displayed rate times the two reflection norms, with the squares centered on a cut included in its reflection kernel.
  - Explanation: Products of twisted rows around a source obey a low bound, improved after subtracting the leading angular mode.
- **claim-plane-kernels** (theorem, [source](#stmt-bulk-plane-kernels)): Finite words of homogeneous normalized strict-angle rows have limiting Gram matrices as $N\to\infty$. Their quotient and completion give a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ with unit vector $\Omega$ and bounded left row actions satisfying $$\label{bulk:row-bound} \\|A^D(\alpha)\\|\le2\\|D\\|.$$ Bare vacuum coefficients are continuous in strict angles and are unchanged by a common translation of all time angles, as long as the translated angles remain in $(-v,v)$.
  - Explanation: Row words have limiting Gram matrices giving a Hilbert space with bounded row actions.
- **claim-angle-generator** (theorem, [source](#stmt-bulk-boost)): There is a self-adjoint operator $B$ on $\mathcal H$ such that $V_th=e^{tB}h$ locally for each word $h$. Ordinary strict-angle words form a graph core for $B$. Each family $A^D$ extends to a bounded holomorphic operator function on $\|\operatorname{Re}z\|<v$, with $$\label{bulk:imaginary-covariance} A^D(x+ib)=U_bA^D(x)U_{-b},\qquad U_b=e^{ibB}.$$
  - Explanation: Angle translation is generated by a self-adjoint operator and row families extend holomorphically.
- **claim-edge-band** (theorem, [source](#stmt-bulk-edge-band)): Almost every spectral function $f$ extends analytically and without zeros to bands of one fixed positive width about the lines $\operatorname{Re}z=\pm v$. It has modulus one on those lines and satisfies $\|f(z)\|\le1$ in the intervening strip. At any specified point of the strip, the set of spectral functions vanishing there has measure zero.
  - Explanation: Scalar spectral functions continue analytically without zeros through bands about both strip edges.
- **claim-path-deformation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cur-deformation)): In the positive winding expansion, the primitive is invariant, pairing by pairing, under simple-path isotopies that continue its initial lift, keep its endpoints in their regions, and avoid the other insertions. The statement is a tensor identity for arbitrary outside spins. A pure diagonal string obeys the corresponding deformation rule without a source.
  - Explanation: The path primitive is invariant under admissible isotopies.
- **claim-tree-weights** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cur-tree-weights)): For an arc $e:i\to j$ bounding its child interval, put $m=h_i-h_j$ and $$\label{cur:weights} \begin{aligned} w_e&=\frac{\cos((m-\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},& k_e&=-\frac{\cos((m+\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},\\ a_e&=e^{-i\lambda(h_i+h_j)},& c_*&=\frac{e^{-i\lambda}}{2\sin\lambda}. \end{aligned}$$ For each fixed pairing, the primitive to $z$ is the sum over a marked edge of the separator-tree path from $p$ to the region of $z$: use $k_e$ on earlier edges, $c_*a_e$ on the marked edge, and $w_e$ on every other boundary arc. Unmarked internal loops have weight $d$, and a marked closed loop contributes zero.* *For a pure $K(Q)$ string to $z$, use $k_e$ on the full separator-tree path and $w_e$ off it. An internal loop enclosing $z$ then has weight $-2$ instead of $d$. The parity of the number of such loops records the color change from the boundary-tree region to the lattice color of $z$.
  - Explanation: The primitive in a disk is evaluated as a sum over separator-tree paths with explicit arc weights.
- **claim-slab-estimate** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cur-slab-estimate)): Suppose a diagonal-time slab of macroscopic thickness about a low or high stencil contains no other non-diagonal tensors or endpoints. Diagonal chains may cross the slab. The stencil has an intact neighborhood disjoint from all other chains except its own prefix, and the slab has spare margins for routing and cuts. Bounded lattice errors are permitted inside these margins. Then the stencil contraction can be written as the corresponding low or high expression in Theorem <a href="#bulk:angular-estimate" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="bulk:angular-estimate">16</a>, between exterior states independent of the choice of stencil term. Only boundedly many compensating pairs of rows and a common bounded scalar are introduced.* *In particular, if the two clear parts of the slab contain at least $n$ physical steps, its scalar contraction is bounded by $Cn^{-1+\rho}$ for a low stencil, and by $Cn^{-1-\rho}$ for a high stencil, times the two exterior reflection norms. Reflected stencils satisfy the same statement.
  - Explanation: Stencils in a clear diagonal slab are bounded by negative powers of the number of steps times exterior norms.
- **claim-four-tree** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-tree)): The number of loops closed by the local boundary caps is $$\mathcal I=\#\{\text{unwired tree vertices}\}. \label{four:loop-count}$$ Exactly one of $E_{\mathfrak A},E_{\mathfrak B}$ occurs. Completing the four open ports around $A,C$ adds respectively one and two loops on these events.* *For an edge $e$ represented by an arc $i\to j$, $i<j$, put $$m_e=h_i-h_j,\qquad w_e=\frac{\cos((m_e-\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},\qquad k_e=-\frac{\cos((m_e+\tfrac12)\lambda)}{\sin\lambda},\qquad a_e=x^{h_i+h_j}. \label{four:edge-weights}$$ Let $\mathcal P(V)$ be the root-to-$V$ edge path. Define $$\begin{aligned} D_V&=d^{-\mathcal I}\prod_{e\in\mathcal P(V)}k_e \prod_{e\notin\mathcal P(V)}w_e,\label{four:D}\\ H_V&=d^{-\mathcal I}\sum_{e\in\mathcal P(V)}a_e \prod_{f\text{ before }e\text{ in }\mathcal P(V)}k_f \prod_{f\text{ not before }e,\ f\ne e}w_f. \label{four:H} \end{aligned}$$ Thus $H_{\rm root}=0$. If $e$ joins its parent $u$ to its child $v$, the common product $D_e^\circ$, with the factor on $e$ omitted, satisfies $$H_v-H_u=a_eD_e^\circ,\qquad D_u=w_eD_e^\circ,\qquad D_v=k_eD_e^\circ. \label{four:recursion}$$
  - Explanation: The cap loop count equals the number of unwired tree vertices and the tree weights are given in recursion form.
- **claim-four-marked** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-marked)): Call the tree *typical* when all four terminal legs have positive length. On a typical tree, $$D_p=D_b=D_{d_0}=0,\qquad \frac{H_b}{P_0G}=\begin{cases}1&E_{\mathfrak A},\\d&E_{\mathfrak B},\end{cases} \quad \frac{H_{d_0}}{P_0G}=y\begin{cases}d&E_{\mathfrak A},\\1&E_{\mathfrak B}. \end{cases} \label{four:marked-values}$$ On the gap visits of any interval $R$, $$\begin{gathered} \Re(H_V/A_R)-c_R(\operatorname{col}(V))D_V \quad\text{is constant},\\ c_R(\text{wire color})=-\cos\lambda,\qquad c_R(\text{other color})=\cos(2\lambda). \end{gathered} \label{four:line-invariant}$$ Set $$\Gamma(\mathfrak A)=P_0y^2,\qquad \Gamma(\mathfrak B)=-P_0y,\qquad H_V^\circ=H_V-\Gamma(\operatorname{col}(V))D_V. \label{four:corrected}$$ The variables $H_V^\circ$ are bounded uniformly over all trees and vertices. On a typical tree they have value $P_0GT$ along the $c$-leg and all its descendant branches, where $$T=\mathbf1_{E_{\mathfrak A}}+y\mathbf1_{E_{\mathfrak B}}. \label{four:T}$$ On gap visits along $B$, their only possible values are $H_b,P_0GT$; along $C$, they are $H_{d_0},P_0GT$.
  - Explanation: Marked values and a bounded corrected observable are computed on typical trees.
- **claim-four-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-compactness)): For every fixed positive power, the moments of $\|H_{V(z)}\|+\|D_{V(z)}\|$ are bounded by a power of $\min(1,\|z-c\|)^{-1}$, uniformly when $z$ is farther than a mesh-scale distance from $c$. The expectations in <a href="#four:observable" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="four:observable">[four:observable]</a> are asymptotically equicontinuous on interior compact sets. Every lattice parity therefore has the same locally continuous subsequential limits.* *Typicality has probability tending to one. As a macroscopic interior point approaches an ordinary boundary point, including a polygon corner, its tree vertex visits that point’s interval with probability tending to one after the mesh limit. Near $b,c,d_0$ it lies beyond an edge of the corresponding terminal leg with high probability; near $p$ an unpassed $L=3$ edge remains with high probability.
  - Explanation: Observable moments are polynomially bounded and boundary shielding holds with high probability.
- **claim-diagonal-residual** (theorem, [source](#stmt-four-residual)): For every bounded function $\gamma$ of the two colors and every boundary point $u$ distinct from the four marks, $$\lim_{z\to u}\limsup_{n\to\infty} \left\|\mathbb E_{\rm open} [\gamma(\operatorname{col}(V(z)))D_{V(z)}]\right\|=0. \label{four:boundary-residual}$$ Here $z$ in the outer limit is a macroscopic interior location, and any lattice vertices tending to it may be used in the inner limit.
  - Explanation: The diagonal residual term vanishes in the limit at unmarked boundary points.
- **claim-conditional-map** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-four-conditional-map)): Suppose an interior subsequential limit $h$ of $h_n$ is holomorphic in the ordinary complex coordinate, and pass simultaneously to a limit $r$ of $P_{\mathfrak A}$. Then $0<r<1$. Put $$U_0=r+d(1-r),\qquad V_0=dr+1-r,\qquad T_0=r+y(1-r). \label{four:target-vertices}$$ The function $h$ maps $\Omega$ conformally onto the interior of the simple polygon with successive vertices $0,U_0,T_0,yV_0$, taking $p,b,c,d_0$ to those vertices. If a conformal half-plane coordinate takes the marks to $0,\chi,1,\infty$, respectively, then $$r=\frac{\displaystyle\int_1^\infty u^{\rho-1}\|u-\chi\|^{\rho-1}\|u-1\|^{1-3\rho}\,du} {\displaystyle\int_\chi^\infty u^{\rho-1}\|u-\chi\|^{\rho-1}\|u-1\|^{1-3\rho}\,du}. \label{four:crossing-formula}$$ Under deterministic separate $\mathfrak A$ caps the corresponding crossing probability is $r/(r+d(1-r))$.
  - Explanation: If a limit is holomorphic, it is a conformal map onto an explicit polygon giving the crossing formula.
- **claim-distant-normalization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-wall-distant)): For sufficiently large fixed $L$, under the exterior positive tilt $\nu_U\propto U\mu$, $$\mathbb E_{\nu_U}(Y/U)\ge c_L>0,\qquad \mathbb E_{\nu_U}\|Y/U\|^p\le C_{p,L} \label{wall:distant-moments}$$ for every fixed $p>0$, uniformly for large $R_0$ and fine mesh.
  - Explanation: The distant charge factor has uniformly positive expectation and bounded moments under the tilt.
- **claim-wall-factorization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-wall-factorization)): For the complete wall, there are probe-independent complex numbers $a_n(R_0,L)$, bounded above and away from zero in modulus for the fixed large $L$, such that $$\mathcal H_{\rm full}(z,u) =a_n(R_0,L)h_n(z)J_n(u)+o(1) \label{wall:factorization-eq}$$ uniformly on interior compact probe sets. The error tends to zero with mesh first and then $R_0\to\infty$. No limit of $a_n$ is asserted or needed.
  - Explanation: For a complete wall the paired observable factorizes into interior and exterior parts times a bounded coefficient.
- **claim-gap-closure** (theorem, [source](#stmt-gap-closure)): Keep the distant charges and their locations fixed. Let $g$ denote the gapped wall and $f$ the wall obtained by closing the specified $h$-gaps, retaining any other gaps and tip factors. There are positive probe-independent numbers $b_n$, bounded above and below, such that $$\mathcal H_g(z,u)=b_n\mathcal H_f(z,u)+o(1) \label{gap:comparison}$$ uniformly on interior compact probe sets. The error vanishes in the mesh limit followed by $h\to0$. Constants may depend on the fixed remaining features. In particular, a second, smaller collection of gaps may be closed before the first collection.
  - Explanation: Closing gaps changes the paired observable by a bounded positive probe-independent factor.
- **claim-reflection-templates** (theorem, [source](#stmt-hol-templates)): For fixed primary gap widths and every $\varepsilon>0$, one can choose finitely many reflection and extraction steps and finitely many secondary gaps so that the expected extracted count of each original marker is at least $1-\varepsilon$. The cuts have strict macroscopic clearances. On any compact set of eligible probe pairs, finitely many such templates suffice, and one may use the union of their secondary gaps. All choices precede the mesh limit.
  - Explanation: Finite reflection templates make almost all stencil copies favorable.
- **claim-mixed-bound** (theorem, [source](#stmt-hol-mixed-bound)): For fixed primary gaps and sufficiently small fixed secondary gaps chosen as in Lemma <a href="#hol:templates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="hol:templates">31</a>, there is $c>0$ such that $$\left\| (\delta_{1,z}^{(2)}+i\delta_{2,z}^{(2)}) \delta_{j,u}^{(2)}\mathcal H_g(z,u)\right\| =O(n^{-2-c}) \label{hol:mixed-decay}$$ uniformly on the eligible compact probe sets. The constants and reflection-tree size may depend on these fixed gaps.
  - Explanation: The mixed difference of the paired observable decays with a strict power saving.
- **claim-holomorphic-disk** (theorem, [source](#stmt-hol-disk)): For every rational orthogonal polygon with the four flat marks and balanced approximations specified above, every locally continuous subsequential limit of $h_n$ is holomorphic. Consequently the boundary identification and crossing formula of Proposition <a href="#four:conditional-map" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="four:conditional-map">27</a> hold without its holomorphicity premise for these polygons.
  - Explanation: Subsequential limits of the observable on rational orthogonal polygons are holomorphic.
- **claim-jordan-transfer** (theorem, [source](#stmt-jordan-transfer)): Consider the marked, uniformly convergent square lattice polygon approximations $(D_n;a_n,b_n,c_n,d_n)$ to a bounded Jordan quadrilateral $(D;a,b,c,d)$ in the four-mark sense of Subsection <a href="#intro:crossings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:crossings">1.3</a>. Keep every edge of the polygon graph random, and separately wire the two closed arcs $a_nb_n$ and $c_nd_n$, with no other primal identifications. If $\psi:D\to\mathbb H$ sends $(a,c,d)$ to $(0,1,\infty)$ and $\chi=\psi(b)$, the probability of an actual open path between these arcs tends to $g(\chi)$.
  - Explanation: The crossing probability transfers to uniformly approximated marked Jordan quadrilaterals.
- **claim-jordan-cardy** (theorem, [source](#stmt-jordan-cardy)): At $q=1$, with every edge, including every boundary edge, sampled independently with probability $1/2$ and with no wiring, the probability of the event $C_n$ defined in Subsection <a href="#intro:crossings" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:crossings">1.3</a> tends to $$\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^\chi [t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,dt} {\displaystyle\int_0^1 [t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,dt}.$$
  - Explanation: At the percolation point the crossing probability tends to Cardy's integral.
- **claim-moving-drawing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-drawing)): The prescribed polygon graph and its Dobrushin strand admit a tile and collar representation in a Jordan polygon $V_n$ such that:* 1. *$V_n$ has the same marked uniform Jordan limit as $D_n$;* 2. *the rounded strand is simple, visits the same ordered local pieces as the prescribed medial strand, and is at curve distance $O(\delta_n)$ from it;* 3. *at every stop for this revealing filtration, the remaining domain is a simple slit disk. Under deterministic cap closure its unrevealed edges have the original conditional FK law, with known open edges contracted and known closed edges deleted;* 4. *primal and dual banks of the prefix have physical access to their corresponding known edges and wire vertices within $O(\delta_n)$. Every completion of the unknown edges embeds its actual paths in the slit disk without crossing the past.* *The construction can use identical domains and caps away from an interval where two additional boundary changes are inserted.
  - Explanation: A compatible simple drawing keeps conditional FK laws at switch-revealing stops.
- **claim-small-interval-asymptotic** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-asymptotic)): For $f$ in <a href="#jordan:functions" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="jordan:functions">[jordan:functions]</a>, $$f(1-\chi)=1-f(\chi),\qquad f(\chi)=c_q\chi^h(1+o(1))\quad(\chi\downarrow0), \qquad c_q>0.$$
  - Explanation: The four-change function is antisymmetric about one half and has a power-law small-interval behavior.
- **claim-moving-slit** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-slit)): Let a four-change strand in $V_n$ be stopped before completing its strand, revealing only the switches it has encountered. Let $U_n$ be its remaining simple slit disk, with the tip as the new starting mark. Consider histories for which a fixed basepoint has a fixed positive disk in $U_n$, and the four prime-end marks in a disk chart normalized at that basepoint remain mutually separated by a fixed positive amount. Then, on these histories, $$\label{moving:limit} \mathbb P_{\mathrm{open}}(E_{\mathrm P}\mid\mathcal F_n) -f(\chi_{U_n})\ \longrightarrow\ 0 \quad\hbox{in probability}.$$ Here $E_{\mathrm P}$ is the primal pairing event, equivalently the actual bridge event after separate primal closure, and $\chi_{U_n}$ is its current ordered cross-ratio. The assertion holds for arbitrary mesh-dependent stopping rules satisfying this localization.
  - Explanation: At localized stops the conditional pairing probability is close to the four-change function of the current cross-ratio.
- **claim-chart-modulus** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-chart-modulus)): Let $u_n$ be the rectangle abscissa just defined. Under the localization in Theorem <a href="#moving:slit" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="moving:slit">38</a>, there is a common modulus tending to zero for the oscillation of $u_n$ on a connected path of vanishing physical diameter, including paths with accesses to the prime boundary. Consequently, for $\beta>0$, a possible primal path starting in $\beta\le u_n\le1-\beta$ cannot reach a known primal-open edge or a primal electrode inside a sufficiently small physical ball.
  - Explanation: The rectangle abscissa has a common modulus of oscillation on short connected paths.
- **claim-deletion-cost** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-deletion)): Fix a history and use separate deterministic primal closure. Deleting a set of still random edges changes the actual crossing probability by at most the probability, in the undeleted conditional law, that an endpoint of a deleted edge reaches either wire interval or its revealed primal bank by an actual open path, allowing one initial test step over the deleted edge. Contact at a wire vertex may have length zero. For a central-band set contained in a ball of radius $r$, this cost is bounded by a quantity tending to zero as $r\downarrow0$, uniformly in the history and center, provided its required outer radius is fixed and the mesh is sufficiently small. The same holds for any fixed finite number of such balls.
  - Explanation: Deleting random edges in small balls changes the crossing probability by a vanishing attachment cost.
- **claim-flag-cost** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-flags)): In a fixed bulk block let $\pi$ be a simple known primal bank path. Choose fixed scales $\ell\ll R_1$, away from its endpoints and the original boundary. Flag a deterministic grid cell of side $\ell$ if, in its annulus from $100\ell$ to $R_1$, the prefix already supplies four cyclically alternating actual arms, its two primal arms being known wired bank paths. If a candidate within $O(\ell)$ of this cell actually connects to an electrode, then six actual alternating arms occur in a cropped annulus from $200\ell$ to $R_1/2$. For a bounded region covered by the deterministic cells, the averaged conditional attachment cost of all flagged cells is at most $$\label{moving:flag-sum} C\ell^{-2}(\ell/R_1)^{2+c_0}=O_{R_1}(\ell^{c_0}).$$ The statement remains valid with one initial test step and with the bounded cap changes in <a href="#moving:odds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="moving:odds">[moving:odds]</a>.
  - Explanation: The averaged attachment cost of flagged cells is small by the six-arm estimate.
- **claim-directed-obstacle** (theorem, [source](#stmt-moving-obstacle)): After removing histories of arbitrarily small probability and allowing an arbitrarily small conditional deletion cost, there is a Jordan polygon $H$ containing the basepoint, selected from a finite list at each fixed accuracy, with the following properties. Its boundary follows the original boundary and explored prefix to that accuracy; away from finitely many protected balls and flagged cells it has fixed positive clearance from all central candidates. As the accuracies decrease, $H$ and $U_n$ have the same pointed kernel limits. Artificial marks in $H$ may be chosen with disk angles arbitrarily close to the corresponding angles in $U_n$.
  - Explanation: A Jordan polygon obstacle with clearance from candidates and matching kernel limits exists.
- **claim-martingale-tests** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-tests)): For every $x>2R+1$, put $$\label{chordal:martingale} M_t(x)=\left(\frac{xg_t'(x)}{g_t(x)-W_t}\right)^h.$$ These processes and their reciprocals are bounded on the stopped range, uniformly in the mesh. For arbitrary stopping rules $0\le\sigma_n\le\tau_n$ in that range and uniformly bounded $\mathcal F_{\sigma_n}$-measurable tests $F_n$, $$\label{chordal:approx-martingale} \mathbb E\!\left[F_n\bigl(M_{\tau_n}(x)-M_{\sigma_n}(x)\bigr)\right] \longrightarrow0$$ under the original single-strand Dobrushin law.
  - Explanation: Loewner test processes are bounded approximate martingales under the Dobrushin law.
- **claim-driver-convergence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-driver)): On every compact capacity interval, the Dobrushin driving functions converge in law, uniformly, to $\sqrt\kappa B_t$, where $B$ is standard Brownian motion and $$\label{chordal:kappa} \kappa=\frac{8}{1+h} =\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$
  - Explanation: Driving functions converge to a scaled Brownian motion.
- **claim-territorial-arms** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-territories)): In a buffered bulk annulus, $m$ disjoint radial medial sublegs force at least $m$ alternating actual primal/dual arms in a further cropped annulus. If only one color is retained, one obtains at least one crossing in a distinct intervening strip per two assignments of that color to successive medial separators.
  - Explanation: Disjoint medial sublegs force alternating actual arms.
- **claim-curve-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-compactness)): The physical Dobrushin strands are tight in the uniform Euclidean curve topology modulo increasing reparametrization. Every subsequential limit has no nonconstant interval on the original boundary, and no interior point is visited three times with nonconstant excursions between consecutive visits.
  - Explanation: Strands are tight and limits have no boundary intervals or triple visits.
- **claim-avoidability** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-avoidability)): At a switch-revealing stop of the Dobrushin exploration, call a component of $U_n\cap A(z;r,R)$ *avoidable* if it does not separate the tip access from the target access inside $U_n$. The conditional probability of a future radial traversal in any avoidable component is bounded by a quantity tending to zero as $r/R\downarrow0$, uniformly over histories and centers, with $r,R$ fixed before the mesh limit and $\delta_n\ll r$.
  - Explanation: Future traversal of avoidable components has vanishing probability.
- **claim-target-no-return** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-target)): After the strand first enters a shrinking initial conformal cap around its target, the probability of a subsequent displacement of fixed positive physical size tends to zero.
  - Explanation: After entering a small cap around the target, macroscopic displacement is unlikely.
- **claim-dense-double-points** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-dense-doubles)): For ordinary chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$, $4<\kappa<8$, almost surely every nonempty open capacity interval contains both visits to some interior self-double point.
  - Explanation: Every capacity interval of chordal SLE contains both visits to an interior double point.
- **claim-small-gates** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-gates)): In a joint subsequential limit of the physical strand and its Loewner driving function, the physical curve cannot enter an open component of a Loewner hull that is disjoint from the Loewner trace and the original boundary.
  - Explanation: The physical curve cannot enter swallowed hull components disjoint from the trace.
- **claim-dobrushin-convergence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-chordal-trace)): For every bounded marked Jordan domain and every marked uniform polygon approximation satisfying Equation <a href="#intro:marked-jordan" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="intro:marked-jordan">[intro:marked-jordan]</a> with the boundary conventions of Subsection <a href="#intro:model" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:model">1.1</a>, the Dobrushin strand converges in law, in the uniform Euclidean oriented-curve topology modulo increasing reparametrization, to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$.
  - Explanation: The Dobrushin strand converges in law to chordal SLE in the uniform curve topology.
- **claim-pocket-law** (theorem, [source](#stmt-peel-factorization)): Conditionally on any finite exploration history, the unqueried switches in its remaining components have the positive cap laws described by their boundaries. Distinct components are conditionally independent. Before two targets split into distinct components their explorations are identical. A strand between successive pocket switches is a portion of one original closed loop.
  - Explanation: Unqueried switches in remaining components have positive cap laws and are conditionally independent.
- **claim-wall-crossings** (theorem, [source](#stmt-peel-wall-rsw)): Fix a buffered corridor of bounded aspect in a normalized disk chart. Its terminal wall intervals lie strictly inside designated homogeneous arcs; one terminal interval may instead be an interior bar. After the mesh limit at this fixed scale, an actual crossing of either prescribed color $X$ has conditional probability bounded below, uniformly in the exploration history and its boundary partitions. At an $X$-wall it reaches an actual wall vertex. At an opposite-color wall it reaches the $X$-corner of an inward wall triangle. In the latter case a segment inside that triangle, ending at the midpoint of its base, completes the crossing to a screen and meets an actual $X$-path only at its starting corner.* *The two-sided bounded-density collar comparison of Section <a href="#sec:preliminaries" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:preliminaries">2</a> holds for such buffered chart collars on a homogeneous wall, with a bounded number of through-wire blocks.
  - Explanation: Buffered corridors have uniformly positive conditional crossing probability up to explored walls.
- **claim-generation-tightness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-peel-passages)): The number of edge-disjoint actual monochromatic cycles surrounding a fixed macroscopic ball in the initial square, and using no deterministic initial wall edge, is tight as the mesh tends to zero. Along finitely many target branches with bounded radial horizons, the number of reference-wall generations defined below is jointly tight.
  - Explanation: Disjoint surrounding cycles and reference-wall generations are tight.
- **claim-peeling-martingales** (theorem, [source](#stmt-peel-martingales)): For $x>0$ beyond these localization bounds, the quantities $$\label{peel:test} M_t(x)=\left(\frac{xg_t'(x)}{g_t(x)-W_t^{\mathbb H}}\right)^h$$ satisfy the approximate martingale identities between arbitrary causal stops on the segment. Tests may include the entire earlier exploration history of finitely many targets. The errors tend to zero after the mesh limit. The assertion concerns the averaged identities for this history law, not a uniform assertion over all deterministic mazes.
  - Explanation: Chordal test quantities are approximate martingales between causal stops in the peeled domain.
- **claim-interior-characteristics** (theorem, [source](#stmt-tree-interior)): Away from $\theta\in\{0,2\pi\}$, every limiting branch has the local characteristics $$\label{tree:sde} \begin{aligned} dW_t&=\sqrt\kappa\,dB_t+ \frac{6-\kappa}{2}\cot(\theta_t/2)\,dt,\\ dO_t&=\cot(\theta_t/2)\,dt,\qquad \theta_t=O_t-W_t. \end{aligned}$$ Here $t$ is that branch’s radial clock; the martingale identities hold relative to the full causal exploration history.
  - Explanation: Away from coincidence limiting branches have the stated driver and forcepoint characteristics.
- **claim-fast-motion-bar** (theorem, [source](#stmt-tree-bar)): There are positive constants $c,C$ with the following property. Start at a causal stop with $\theta<r/16$, where $r>0$ is small. For $0<u\ll r^2$, the probability that $W$ advances counterclockwise by $r$ within additional radial time $u$, while $\theta<r/16$ until that advance, is at most $$\label{tree:bar-bound} C\exp(-cr/\sqrt u)+o(1).$$ The error vanishes in the mesh limit for fixed $r,u$. The constants in the limiting estimate are uniform in these parameters. Near $2\pi$ reverse the direction of motion and exchange the colors.
  - Explanation: Fast driver advance near coincidence has exponentially small probability.
- **claim-endpoint-reflection** (theorem, [source](#stmt-tree-reflection)): In its own radial clock, the limiting gap is the unique instantaneous reflected diffusion on $[0,2\pi]$ with interior generator $$\label{tree:generator} \mathcal A f(\theta)=\frac\kappa2 f''(\theta) +\frac{\kappa-4}{2}\cot(\theta/2)f'(\theta).$$ The forcepoint has no singular push: $$\label{tree:no-push} O_t=O_0+\int_0^t\cot(\theta_s/2)\,ds.$$ Equation <a href="#tree:sde" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="tree:sde">[tree:sde]</a> consequently holds globally, including collisions, with locally integrable drift.
  - Explanation: The angular gap is the instantaneous reflected diffusion with no singular push.
- **claim-joint-tree-law** (theorem, [source](#stmt-tree-joint-law)): For every finite family of deterministic interior targets, the peeling converges in its joint radial driving data to the target-invariant branching radial $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa(\kappa-6)$ tree. Branches agree until their target kernels separate and then have independent continuation noises. At successive full turns the force side is reversed, equivalently the angular gap remains instantaneously reflected on $[0,2\pi]$.
  - Explanation: Joint peeling converges to the branching radial tree with independent continuation after separation.
- **claim-loop-geometry** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-geometry)): The closed loop collections in the fixed square are tight for matching uniform curves modulo reparametrization and orientation. Constant limit curves may be removed. Their positive-diameter subsequential limits have the following properties almost surely.* 1. *Each deterministic interior point lies on no loop. Its absolute winding number about any loop is $0$ or $1$, and is stable along a converging loop sequence.* 2. *No interior point has three distinct visits in total among the loop elements. Visits include multiple traversals after constant pauses are removed and also multiplicity of different elements.* 3. *At every interior point of a positive loop, every neighborhood contains open disks of both absolute winding statuses for that loop.
  - Explanation: Loop collections in the square are tight with regular limiting geometry.
- **claim-loop-continuation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-continuation)): At an interior-angle time $s\in(a_k,b_k)$, the remaining traversal of $\widetilde L_z^k$ is the default strand from $W_s$ to $O_s$ in the current domain. In a chart sending those accesses to $0,\infty$, every finite portion of this continuation is ordinary chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ and is recorded by branches to targets from $\mathcal Z$ that remain accessible high above that portion. Every open nonconstant traversal interval of $\widetilde L_z^k$ contains two visits to one square-interior point.
  - Explanation: The remaining traversal is an ordinary chordal strand and nonconstant intervals contain double visits.
- **claim-episode-order** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-episode-order)): As long as the target is macroscopically separated from a consumed tile or star, an episode is successful exactly when its terminal switch changes wall polarity. These polarity changes enumerate all loops surrounding the target, in their order from outside inward. A positive loop with positive clearance from the target is reached before a finite radial horizon depending on that clearance. Conversely a successful switch by a bounded horizon has macroscopic clearance from the target.
  - Explanation: Polarity changes enumerate loops surrounding the target from outside inward.
- **claim-no-skipped-resets** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-no-skip)): At a bounded-clock completed state with $\theta$ approaching $0$, the probability of returning to a fixed positive angle before a primal-pocket reset tends to zero, with the mesh limit first and the endpoint tolerance second. The analogous assertion near $2\pi$ uses a dual-pocket reset. Consequently the true successive discrete polarity-change times $b_k^n$ converge in probability to $b_k$ on sufficiently large finite horizons.* *Moreover, in an episode that succeeds by a bounded horizon, after a fixed interior-angle advance the probability of retreating arbitrarily near its starting endpoint before its successful switch tends to zero in the same order of limits.
  - Explanation: Endpoint resets are not skipped, so discrete polarity-change times converge.
- **claim-ordered-containment** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-ordered)): For each $z\in\mathcal Z$ and $k\ge1$, the entire traversal of $\widetilde L_z^k$ occurs in cyclic order in $L_z^k$, possibly with extra traversal portions inserted. Its order occupies at most one turn of $L_z^k$. If two canonical labels give the same element, their lattice-limit labels give the same collection element.
  - Explanation: Each canonical traversal sits in cyclic order inside its lattice-limit loop.
- **claim-label-equivalence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-label-equivalence)): With equality understood as equality of collection elements, almost surely and simultaneously for all $z,w\in\mathcal Z$ and $k,j\ge1$, $$\label{loop:label-iff} L_z^k=L_w^j \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widetilde L_z^k=\widetilde L_w^j.$$
  - Explanation: Lattice-limit labels coincide exactly when canonical labels coincide.
- **claim-loop-identification** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-identification)): Every positive lattice-limit loop with an interior point has a canonical label. Matched elements have the same winding indicators on $\mathcal Z$. If either matched element stays away from the square wall, the two elements are equal as curves modulo reparametrization and orientation. Without that restriction, every canonical element is still contained in order in its lattice-limit partner.
  - Explanation: Away from the wall lattice-limit loops equal canonical loops as curves.
- **claim-nested-plane-convergence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-loop-plane)): For every fixed $1\le q<4$, the loop collection of the free infinite-volume critical square-lattice FK law converges, through the full mesh sequence, to the nested whole-plane $\mathrm{CLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ in the spherical loop-matching topology of Subsection <a href="#intro:collections" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="intro:collections">1.2</a>. The limit is Möbius invariant and includes every nested generation.
  - Explanation: Free-plane loop collections converge to nested whole-plane CLE in the spherical matching topology.

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-bulk-angular-estimate",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a compact interval $I\\subset(-v,v)$. Let $B_{\\rm in}$ be a product of $P_\\zeta$ rows and $B_{\\rm out}$ a product of $P_\\xi$ rows, at real angles in $[-v,v]$. Suppose each product contains at least $n\\ge1$ angles in $I$. Uniformly for $x,y\\in[-v,v]$, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\|B_{\\rm out}N(x)B_{\\rm in}\\|&\\le Cn^{-1+\\rho},\n \\label{bulk:low-estimate}\\\\\n \\|B_{\\rm out}\\{N(x)-e^{i\\tau(x-y)}N(y)\\}B_{\\rm in}\\|\n &\\le Cn^{-1-\\rho}.\\label{bulk:high-estimate}\n\\end{aligned}$$ The constant depends on $q$ and $I$. Boundedly many additional pairs of before-twist rows may be inserted immediately to the right of $N$, and additional pairs of after-twist rows immediately to its left. The two terms in <a href=\"#bulk:high-estimate\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"bulk:high-estimate\">[bulk:high-estimate]</a> may use different such insertions; on each side their counts must be even. The constant may depend on a bound for these counts.         "anchor": "stmt-cur-slab-estimate",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose a diagonal-time slab of macroscopic thickness about a low or high stencil contains no other non-diagonal tensors or endpoints. Diagonal chains may cross the slab. The stencil has an intact neighborhood disjoint from all other chains except its own prefix, and the slab has spare margins for routing and cuts. Bounded lattice errors are permitted inside these margins. Then the stencil contraction can be written as the corresponding low or high expression in Theorem <a href=\"#bulk:angular-estimate\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"bulk:angular-estimate\">16</a>, between exterior states independent of the choice of stencil term. Only boundedly many compensating pairs of rows and a common bounded scalar are introduced.*\n\n*In particular, if the two clear parts of the slab contain at least $n$ physical steps, its scalar contraction is bounded by $Cn^{-1+\\rho}$ for a low stencil, and by $Cn^{-1-\\rho}$ for a high stencil, times the two exterior reflection norms. Completing the four open ports around $A,C$ adds respectively one and two loops on these events.*\n\n\n\n\n\n*For an edge $e$ represented by an arc $i\\to j$, $i<j$, put $$m_e=h_i-h_j,\\qquad\n w_e=\\frac{\\cos((m_e-\\tfrac12)\\lambda)}{\\sin\\lambda},\\qquad\n k_e=-\\frac{\\cos((m_e+\\tfrac12)\\lambda)}{\\sin\\lambda},\\qquad\n a_e=x^{h_i+h_j}.\n \\label{four:edge-weights}$$ Let $\\mathcal P(V)$ be the root-to-$V$ edge path. Define $$\\begin{aligned}\n D_V&=d^{-\\mathcal I}\\prod_{e\\in\\mathcal P(V)}k_e\n                         \\prod_{e\\notin\\mathcal P(V)}w_e,\\label{four:D}\\\\\n H_V&=d^{-\\mathcal I}\\sum_{e\\in\\mathcal P(V)}a_e\n       \\prod_{f\\text{ before }e\\text{ in }\\mathcal P(V)}k_f\n       \\prod_{f\\text{ not before }e,\\ f\\ne e}w_f.\n       \\label{four:H}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Thus $H_{\\rm root}=0$. If $e$ joins its parent $u$ to its child $v$, the common product $D_e^\\circ$, with the factor on $e$ omitted, satisfies $$H_v-H_u=a_eD_e^\\circ,\\qquad\n D_u=w_eD_e^\\circ,\\qquad D_v=k_eD_e^\\circ.\n \\label{four:recursion}$$",

        "anchor": "stmt-moving-flags",
        "exact_quote": "In a fixed bulk block let $\\pi$ be a simple known primal bank path. Choose fixed scales $\\ell\\ll R_1$, away from its endpoints and the original boundary. Flag a deterministic grid cell of side $\\ell$ if, in its annulus from $100\\ell$ to $R_1$, the prefix already supplies four cyclically alternating actual arms, its two primal arms being known wired bank paths. If a candidate within $O(\\ell)$ of this cell actually connects to an electrode, then six actual alternating arms occur in a cropped annulus from $200\\ell$ to $R_1/2$.         "anchor": "stmt-peel-wall-rsw",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a buffered corridor of bounded aspect in a normalized disk chart. Its terminal wall intervals lie strictly inside designated homogeneous arcs; one terminal interval may instead be an interior bar. After the mesh limit at this fixed scale, an actual crossing of either prescribed color $X$ has conditional probability bounded below, uniformly in the exploration history and its boundary partitions. At an $X$-wall it reaches an actual wall vertex. At an opposite-color wall it reaches the $X$-corner of an inward wall triangle. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **critical edge probability p_q** ([source](#intro:finite-law)): Fix a real number $1\le q<4$ and put $$\label{intro:parameters} p_q=\frac{\sqrt q}{1+\sqrt q}, \qquad \kappa(q)=\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$ The inverse cosine has values in $[0,\pi]$. Thus $4<\kappa(q)\le6$, with $\kappa(1)=6$ and $\kappa(q)\downarrow4$ as $q\uparrow4$. On a finite graph $G=(V,E)$, let $\xi$ be a partition of designated boundary vertices. For $A\subseteq E$, let $k_\xi(A)$ be the number of components of $(V,A)$ after identification within each block of $\xi$, including isolated vertices. The random-cluster law is $$\label{intro:finite-law} \phi_{G,q}^{\xi}(A) =\frac{1}{Z_{G,q}^{\xi}} p_q^{\|A\|}(1-p_q)^{\|E\|-\|A\|}q^{k_\xi(A)}.$$ An *actual open path* always consists of open edges of $G$. Identification in $\xi$ is used to compute the probability weight and does not supply an additional edge in such a path.
- **random-cluster law on a finite graph** ([source](#intro:finite-law)): Fix a real number $1\le q<4$ and put $$\label{intro:parameters} p_q=\frac{\sqrt q}{1+\sqrt q}, \qquad \kappa(q)=\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$ The inverse cosine has values in $[0,\pi]$. Thus $4<\kappa(q)\le6$, with $\kappa(1)=6$ and $\kappa(q)\downarrow4$ as $q\uparrow4$. On a finite graph $G=(V,E)$, let $\xi$ be a partition of designated boundary vertices. For $A\subseteq E$, let $k_\xi(A)$ be the number of components of $(V,A)$ after identification within each block of $\xi$, including isolated vertices. The random-cluster law is $$\label{intro:finite-law} \phi_{G,q}^{\xi}(A) =\frac{1}{Z_{G,q}^{\xi}} p_q^{\|A\|}(1-p_q)^{\|E\|-\|A\|}q^{k_\xi(A)}.$$ An *actual open path* always consists of open edges of $G$. Identification in $\xi$ is used to compute the probability weight and does not supply an additional edge in such a path.
- **curve metric** ([source](#intro:curve-metric)): For continuous oriented curves $\gamma_1,\gamma_2:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$, write $$\label{intro:curve-metric} d_{\mathrm{curv}}(\gamma_1,\gamma_2) =\inf_{\varphi_1,\varphi_2} \sup_{0\le t\le1} \|\gamma_1(\varphi_1(t))-\gamma_2(\varphi_2(t))\|,$$ where the infimum is over increasing homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$. Zero-distance curves are identified. Chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_\kappa$ in $(D;a,b)$ is the conformal image of the upper-half-plane Loewner trace driven by $\sqrt\kappa B_t$ from $0$ to $\infty$, with $B$ a standard Brownian motion. The remaining positive dilation of the conformal coordinate does not change this law.
- **loop weight and angle parameters** ([source](#intro:lambda-rho)): $$\label{intro:lambda-rho} d=\sqrt q=2\cos\lambda,\qquad \rho=\lambda/\pi,\qquad 0<\lambda\le\pi/3.$$ The first part of the proof determines an alternating-boundary connection probability. Four marked points divide the boundary into arcs $A,B,C,D$, with the first and third assigned one color and the other two the opposite color. We study the event of an actual path of the first color from $A$ to $C$. Section <a href="#sec:fourchange" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:fourchange">6</a> defines the auxiliary finite law with four unmatched medial ends and no extra pairing weights, and computes its limiting probability $f(\chi)$ when the boundary marks have half-plane coordinates $0,\chi,1,\infty$, $0<\chi<1$. Completing the two designated arcs by separate deterministic wires gives instead $f/(f+d(1-f))$. We keep this normalization change explicit before returning to actual FK crossings.
- **logarithmic comparison parameters** ([source](#exp:parameters)): $$\label{exp:parameters} \Delta=\frac{\pi}{2\lambda}-\frac32,\qquad s=\Delta+1,\qquad t=-\Delta,\qquad f(g)=\frac{\sin((2-g)\lambda)\sin((1+g)\lambda)} {\sin(2\lambda)\sin\lambda}.$$ In the local experiments below, the cutoff radius is comparable to $n$ in mesh units, the specified local geometry extends beyond it by a fixed buffer, and the exterior has any fixed compatible positive completion.
- **four-change functions f and g** ([source](#jordan:functions)): Throughout Sections <a href="#sec:jordan" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:jordan">10</a>–<a href="#sec:chordal" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:chordal">12</a>, fix $1\le q<4$ and write $$d=\sqrt q=2\cos\lambda,\qquad \rho=\lambda/\pi, \qquad h=1-2\rho\in[1/3,1).$$ The four-change calculation of Section <a href="#sec:fourchange" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:fourchange">6</a>, whose holomorphicity hypothesis is supplied in Section <a href="#sec:holomorphic" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:holomorphic">9</a>, gives the functions $$\label{jordan:functions} f(\chi)=\frac{I_C(\chi)}{I_B(\chi)+I_C(\chi)},\qquad g(\chi)=\frac{f(\chi)}{f(\chi)+d(1-f(\chi))}, \quad 0<\chi<1,$$ where $$\begin{aligned} I_B(\chi)&=\int_\chi^1 u^{\rho-1}(u-\chi)^{\rho-1}(1-u)^{1-3\rho}\,du, \\ I_C(\chi)&=\int_1^\infty u^{\rho-1}(u-\chi)^{\rho-1}(u-1)^{1-3\rho}\,du. \end{aligned}$$ The first function is the probability in the open-cap normalization; the second is the probability of an *actual open path* between the two separately wired intervals. Wiring changes component weights; it does not supply an open path between different intervals.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-loop-law** [claim](#stmt-prelim-loop-law) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-loop-law): Euler formula on thickened open graph -> loop weight proportional to FK weight
- **step-collar** [claim](#stmt-prelim-collar) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-collar): likelihood-ratio monotonicity and screening searches -> bounded densities across collars
- **step-passages** [claim](#stmt-prelim-passages) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-passages): component exploration with geometric tail -> exponential passage moments
- **step-tilts** [claim](#stmt-prelim-tilts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prelim-tilts): Jensen and Hölder induction on levels -> tilted moment bounds
- **step-cap-elimination** [claim](#stmt-exp-cap-elimination) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-cap-elimination): inside-out arc removal -> cap loop factors
- **step-log-budgets** [claim](#stmt-exp-comparisons) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-cap-elimination-2): compare two winding expansions on rectangle and cylinders -> logarithmic budget inequalities
- **step-angular** [claim](#stmt-bulk-angular-estimate) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bulk-edge-band): spectral analysis of commuting rows and Laurent modes -> angular decay estimates
- **step-four-tree** [claim](#stmt-four-tree) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-tree): boundary-arc tree computation -> tree observable
- **step-four-residual** [claim](#stmt-four-residual) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-residual): weighted residual cancellation and decoupling -> boundary values
- **step-wall-factorization** [claim](#stmt-wall-factorization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-wall-factorization): paired wall and exterior tilt -> interior-exterior factorization
- **step-gap-closure** [claim](#stmt-gap-closure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-gap-closure): confinement and local multiplier -> gap closure comparison
- **step-templates** [claim](#stmt-hol-templates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hol-templates): martingale purity of folded words -> favorable copies
- **step-mixed** [claim](#stmt-hol-mixed-bound) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hol-mixed-bound): combine extraction decay with budget -> mixed difference saving
- **step-holomorphic** [claim](#stmt-hol-disk) / [proof](#proof-stmt-hol-disk): distributional limit and test pairing -> holomorphic limit
- **step-conditional-map** [claim](#stmt-four-conditional-map) / [proof](#proof-stmt-four-conditional-map): argument principle and Schwarz–Christoffel -> conformal map onto polygon
- **step-jordan-transfer** [claim](#stmt-jordan-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-jordan-transfer): easier and harder comparison quads -> crossing limit in Jordan quadrilaterals
- **step-moving-slit** [claim](#stmt-moving-slit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-moving-obstacle-2): obstacle construction and fiber matching -> moving four-change test
- **step-chordal-tests** [claim](#stmt-chordal-tests) / [proof](#proof-stmt-chordal-tests): insert small wired interval -> bounded martingale tests
- **step-driver** [claim](#stmt-chordal-driver) / [proof](#proof-stmt-chordal-driver): two-test convexity and Lévy characterization -> Brownian driver
- **step-dobrushin** [claim](#stmt-chordal-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-chordal-trace): driver, compactness and plateau exclusion -> curve convergence
- **step-peel-martingales** [claim](#stmt-peel-martingales) / [proof](#proof-stmt-peel-martingales): notch construction and moving-domain comparison -> peeling tests
- **step-reflection** [claim](#stmt-tree-reflection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-tree-reflection): Bessel dimension and block variation bound -> no singular push
- **step-joint-tree** [claim](#stmt-tree-joint-law) / [proof](#proof-stmt-tree-joint-law): common clocks and Knight's theorem -> branching tree law
- **step-loop-identification** [claim](#stmt-loop-identification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loop-identification): label equivalence and traversal order -> canonical loop identification
- **step-plane** [claim](#stmt-loop-plane) / [proof](#proof-stmt-loop-plane): square-to-plane coupling and escape bounds -> whole-plane CLE convergence

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **inv-kappa-from-rho**: For the fixed parameter range, the Loewner diffusion constant satisfies kappa = 8/(1+h) with h = 1-2*rho and rho = lambda/pi, which is the same as kappa = 4/(1-rho); at the right end of the range rho = 1/3 this gives kappa = 6.
- **inv-boundary-exponent-range**: The exponent h = 1-2*rho lies in the stated interval for every admissible rho, so the extremal ends of the parameter interval give the extremal values of h and kappa.
- **inv-alternating-arm-exponent**: The alternating 2k-arm exponent of square-lattice bond percolation is (4k^2-1)/12, an exact rational that depends only on k.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-uniform-in-q**: Using the constants kappa(q), h or the limiting statements as if they were uniform as q approaches the upper end of the interval, or at the endpoint itself. -> The estimates behind the statements are only proved at each fixed q below the endpoint; constants may degenerate and the endpoint is outside the result.
- **anti-cardy-wiring**: Applying the crossing-probability formula to a crossing event defined with wired boundary arcs or with external connections added. -> The formula is for an actual open path with every edge, including boundary edges, sampled freely; wiring changes the event and the limiting value.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `algorithmic`. The paper's proved scaling limits are not finite procedures, but the explicit parameter relations (kappa = 8/(1+h), h = 1-2*rho, kappa(1) = 6) and the alternating-arm exponent (4k^2-1)/12 are closed-form rational expressions that a finite exact-arithmetic procedure computes; only these finite identities are checked, not any limit theorem.

```python
# INPUTS: one line with three integers a b k, meaning rho = a/b and arm index k
# PRECONDITIONS: 0 < rho <= 1/3 and k >= 1; otherwise the output is the word INVALID
# OUTPUTS: one line with exact fractions kappa, h, arm exponent for 2k arms; or INVALID
# TIME: constant number of big-integer operations in the bit length of the input
# SPACE: constant number of big integers
# ARITHMETIC: exact rationals via fractions.Fraction, no floating point
# FAILURE: out-of-range rho or k prints INVALID; malformed input raises and exits nonzero
import sys
from fractions import Fraction


def main():
    a, b, k = (int(t) for t in sys.stdin.read().split())
    rho = Fraction(a, b)
    if rho <= 0 or rho > Fraction(1, 3) or k < 1:
        print("INVALID")
        return
    h = 1 - 2 * rho
    kappa = Fraction(8) / (1 + h)
    arm = Fraction(4 * k * k - 1, 12)
    print(kappa, h, arm)


main()
```

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-q-range-fixed** (formal_scope): The interface and loop convergence is proved separately at each fixed cluster weight in the half-open interval from 1 up to but excluding 4; no uniformity across q is asserted. Blocked use: ['Using constants or limit statements as if uniform as q approaches 4', 'Interchanging a limit in q with the mesh limit']
- **limit-endpoint-q-four** (edge_case): The estimates of the preliminary section are not asserted uniformly as q increases to 4, and q = 4 itself is outside the proof. Blocked use: ['Applying the strict angular or six-arm estimates at q = 4', 'Quoting the exponent kappa(q) bounds as valid at the endpoint']
- **limit-cardy-free-boundary** (hypothesis): Cardy's formula is proved for the actual-path crossing event with every edge, boundary edges included, sampled independently and no wiring, under the stated approximation conventions. Blocked use: ['Using the formula for crossing events defined with wired arcs or external connections', 'Using it with approximations that do not satisfy the marked uniform convergence']
- **limit-exponents-bond-only** (formal_scope): The arm and thermodynamic exponents are derived only for independent square-lattice bond percolation at the critical point, for even cyclically alternating arm words. Blocked use: ['Transferring the exponent values to q different from 1', 'Using the arm formula for odd or non-alternating color words']
- **limit-holomorphicity-rational-polygons** (hypothesis): Holomorphicity of subsequential limits of the four-change observable is proved only for rational orthogonal polygons with flat marks and balanced approximations; general domains need the separate transfer step. Blocked use: ['Applying the holomorphic identification directly to an arbitrary Jordan domain', 'Dropping the rationality or balanced-corner requirement']
- **limit-conditional-map-premise** (hypothesis): The conformal-map and crossing-formula identification is conditional on the limit being holomorphic; it is not unconditional. Blocked use: ['Using the polygon map or crossing formula without first establishing holomorphicity']
- **limit-jordan-transfer-marked-approximation** (hypothesis): The Jordan-quadrilateral transfer requires marked, uniformly convergent square-lattice polygon approximations and separate wiring of the two designated arcs. <a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every fixed $`1\le q\lt 4`$, critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge as ordered curves to chordal $`\mathop{\mathrm{SLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$, where $`\kappa(q)=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)`$, confirming the Rohde–Schramm prediction in this parameter range. This holds in every bounded Jordan domain under uniform marked boundary approximation. The complete nested plane loop collections converge to whole-plane $`\mathop{\mathrm{CLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}`$ in a spherical matching topology retaining multiplicities and traversals. At <i>q</i> = 1 we obtain Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.
